title: chains: H-bond chains, multi-criterion distribution
purpose: Exercises `chains` [@epsrmanual], which finds chains of bonded molecules with the shortest-path criterion of Franzblau [@franzblau1991] as cited in the Fortran: a bond requires an atom1-atom2 pair in one molecule and atom3 in another within three distance windows (and optionally an atom2-atom1-atom3 angle range); chains start at molecules with one neighbour, and histograms of neighbour numbers and chain lengths are written.
system: Analysed configuration: `200DMSO400Water.ato`, an unchanged copy of the EPSR-test box of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO; atom types S, O, C, H) and 400 water molecules (O1, H1): 3200 atoms, DMSO mole fraction 1/3, 300 K, cubic box of side 33.1213 Å (0.0881 atoms/Å³), the EPSR model of the deuterated DMSO-water neutron data (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), cf. [@soperluzar1992]. Distribution 1: water-water hydrogen bonds O1(-H1)···O1 with O-H 0.8-1.2 Å, O···O 2.5-3.3 Å, H···O 1.5-2.4 Å and H-O···O angle 0-30°. Distribution 2: two criteria (`iw` loop), `O1 H1 O*` (`*` matches DMSO O and water O1, angle 0-35°) and `O1 H1 S` (0-180°, angle test skipped because the cosine range is >= 1.9). Reference `fort.14`: mean neighbour numbers 1.37 and 2.25.
inputs: `hbchain.CHAINS.dat`: `nsize 40`, `nsumt 0`, two distributions as above. `200DMSO400Water.ato` copied unchanged from EPSR-test; the keyword file was written by hand (the Fortran program creates no template when the named file does not exist; keywords and defaults from `setup_symbols_generic.f`).
verification: `repeat 2` with `nsumt 0` (accumulation over the two runs; reference `nsumt 2`). Exercises the bond search, `shortest_path`, the chain search and both histograms. Compared after each pass: `hbchain.CHAINS.n01`, the rewritten `hbchain.CHAINS.dat`, and `fort.14` (mean and spread of each histogram, written after unit 14 was closed, see ex60). The configuration is the same in every pass, so the chained passes test the read-back of the accumulated file and the running-average arithmetic.
